payingUser: A coin collector who already keeps the collection in a paper album or a spreadsheet and wants the record searchable on the phone he carries to a fair, a coin shop or a club meeting.
paidUnit: One permanent unlock of the full catalogue: unlimited coins, several collections, photos, search and filters, per-collection totals and CSV export, with no subscription and no advertising.
momentOfPayment: After the collector has entered his first coins for free, at the moment he wants a twelfth coin, a second collection, or the CSV export, behind one clearly priced unlock sheet.
distinctnessSentence: A collector can find a coin by year and denomination in seconds, edit it, photograph it and delete a coin he sold in one tap, and own the whole record as a CSV file with no account and no subscription, which the measured incumbents do not offer.
day1RevenuePath: The slot is listed on Play against the collection-catalogue query where the free leader com.spencerpages holds 500K+ installs at 4.3 stars, the first collectors install it, the free limit stops them at eleven coins, and the first unlock payment arrives through the billing capability the plan requires.
assumptionsUnverified: Install-to-purchase conversion is assumed at 2 percent of installs; no slot in this repository has ever measured a real conversion rate, so every revenue figure derived from it is an assumption.

The collector audience is assumed to pay for cataloguing at all: the measured catalogue leader declares no in-app purchases, and the paying apps in the measured shelf sell coin identification rather than record keeping.

Google Play's 15 percent service fee, a 2 percent refund allowance and a 2 percent currency-conversion allowance are plan assumptions in docs/monetization-strategy.md section 2.2, not measurements of this developer account.
The install bucket behind the leader is a bound rather than a point: a 500K+ figure spans five hundred thousand to nine hundred thousand lifetime installs.
Search ranking is unknown: the collection query is dominated by identification apps, including one at 10M+ installs, so a catalogue has to outrank them rather than only beat the second result.
